case_title: Sharanjit Kaur & Anr. v. State of Punjab
statutory_provisions: IPC s.420 (the only offence in issue). Punjab Panchayati Raj Act, 1994 ss.4(2), 5, 44-51, 71, 77 were invoked on jurisdiction, not as charges.
evidence_type: Documentary: complainant's complaint and affidavit; dishonoured cheque of Rs. 30 lakhs. No witness evidence was assessed by the Court.
aggravating_circumstances: Allegations of serious nature; alleged fraud of Rs. 30 lakhs on a complainant who sold property to raise funds.
trial_court_outcome: No trial reported. The Additional Sessions Judge, Amritsar dismissed the anticipatory bail applications.
high_court_outcome: Anticipatory bail petitions dismissed (23.07.2012); writ petition for restraint of arrest dismissed (07.11.2012).
neutral_facts: The complainant alleged that the accused had taken about Rs. 30 lakhs from him on the promise of arranging a permanent job abroad for his son. The complainant said the money was paid in several instalments, and that he sold property and raised funds to pay it. When the promised job did not materialise and repeated requests for repayment were not met, the accused issued a cheque for Rs. 30 lakhs, which was dishonoured for insufficient funds. The complainant lodged a First Information Report at the police station, which was registered under the cheating provision of the Indian Penal Code. The complainant later filed an affidavit setting out these details. The State maintained that the allegations were serious, that the accused had not joined earlier enquiry proceedings despite repeated calls, and that the police could investigate the offence. No witness statements or other investigation findings are reported in the judgment.
financial_property_loss: Rs. 30 lakhs (alleged), paid by the complainant in instalments; cheque for Rs. 30 lakhs dishonoured
motive: alleged: obtaining money by promising a permanent job abroad for the complainant's son
key_evidence_accepted: No evidence was tested. The Court relied on the serious nature of the allegations in the FIR and complainant's affidavit only to hold that the offence should be tried by a criminal court.
post_offence_conduct: Not stated (this was the State's submission; the Court did not find it)
bail_history: Anticipatory bail refused by Additional Sessions Judge (19.04.2012 and 18.05.2012) and High Court (23.07.2012). Supreme Court stayed arrest of co-accused Sharanjit Kaur and Mukhtiar Singh on 21.09.2012. Interim protection vacated by this judgment.
trial_duration: offence: not given (FIR lodged 03.04.2012); trial judgment: not given; High Court: 23.07.2012 and 07.11.2012; Supreme Court: 01.07.2013
legal_representation: Appellants: R.K. Kapoor. State: Ajay Kapur, AAG. Amicus curiae: A.S. Chandhiok, ASG.
investigation_status: FIR No. 17 registered on 03.04.2012; investigation ongoing and to be conducted by police
appeal_history: Trial court: not applicable (no trial; anticipatory bail dismissed). High Court: petitions dismissed. Supreme Court: appeals dismissed.
prosecution_argument: Given the serious allegations of cheating and fraud, the prosecution may proceed under the IPC despite the Panchayati Raj Act; criminal courts have no bar, and police may investigate.
defence_argument: Under the Punjab Panchayati Raj Act, the Gram Panchayat has complete power to take cognizance of criminal cases, so the IPC proceedings are not sustainable and no investigation can be carried out by police.
legal_principle_applied: Police investigation is not barred; Gram Panchayat has no jurisdiction until investigation is complete; without transfer under s.45 PPR Act, it gets no jurisdiction unless s.47(3) applies; police powers cannot be abridged.
precedent_relied_upon: Distinguished as not helpful: State of M.P. v. Shobharam AIR 1966 SC 1910; Bhim Sen v. State of U.P. AIR 1955 SC 435; Meena Ram v. Master Dwarki AIR 1958 Punjab 417; Chhotey Lal v. State AIR 1967 All 229. Referred to: Giani Ram v. Attar Chand AIR 1960 Punjab 80; Baldeo Singh v. State of Bihar AIR 1957 SC 612; Kartar Singh v. Pritam Singh AIR 1956 Pepsu 78.
judicial_aggravating_factors: Seriousness of the allegations and the alleged fraud of Rs. 30 lakhs
other_sentence_order: Interim protection vacated; offence under s.420 IPC to be tried by regular criminal court, not Gram Panchayat
